# TV Recents

A recent apps screen for rooted Android TV devices. Android TV has no built-in app switcher on many
devices, so this adds one based on the TV Recents screen that was once part of AOSP. Double-press
Home to open it.

> [!WARNING]
> **Root is required.** This is a Magisk module that changes system configuration, and it will not
> work without root.
>
> **This is alpha software, tested on one device.** Installing it reboots your device, and a bad
> module can stop a device from booting. Make sure you know how to recover yours first.

## Requirements

- Root with [Magisk](https://github.com/topjohnwu/Magisk) (tested on 30.7)
- Android TV or Google TV on Android 14

The only tested device is the onn 4K Streaming Device (`wayne`). Other Android 14 TV devices may
work, but that hasn't been tested. See [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md) for exactly what has been.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Home twice | Open Recents, or close it if it's open |
| Guide | Open or close Recents (onn `wayne` only for now) |
| Left / Right | Move between apps (older apps are to the left) |
| Select | Switch to the app |
| Down, then Select | Dismiss the app (Up or Back cancels) |
| Back | Close Recents |

## Install

Download the zip from [Releases](../../releases), then install it with ADB and reboot:

```sh
adb push tvrecents-*.zip /data/local/tmp/tvrecents.zip
adb shell 'su -c "magisk --install-module /data/local/tmp/tvrecents.zip"'
adb shell rm /data/local/tmp/tvrecents.zip
adb reboot
```

You can also install the zip from the Modules tab in the Magisk app.

## Uninstall

Remove it from the Magisk app, or run:

```sh
adb shell 'su -c "touch /data/adb/modules/tvrecents/remove"'
adb reboot
```

## Recovery

If boot never completes three times in a row, the module writes its own `disable` flag, and the next
boot should run without it. This safeguard has not been triggered in testing, so don't rely on it
alone. By hand, delete `/data/adb/modules/tvrecents` from a root shell.

## Known limits

- An app shows its banner until you've left it with Home or opened Recents with Guide over it. Leaving with Back doesn't
  capture a thumbnail.
- DRM video should capture as black, so those apps are expected to show their banner.
- Thumbnails are cleared on reboot.
- After a reboot, a restored card opens the app from its launcher entry, not at its previous screen.
- Single Home presses take 300 ms longer, because Android waits to see if a second press follows.
- Double-pressing Home no longer opens the PiP menu.
- Other remotes need to send `KEY_HOMEPAGE`.
- The Guide button only opens Recents on the onn `wayne`, because each device has its own global key
  table. On that device, Guide no longer goes to Google's launcher.

## How it works

- **Trigger:** some TV builds of SystemUI have no Recents code, so the system's own Recents action
  does nothing. `homewatch.awk` runs as root and reads `getevent` to spot a double-press. It only
  listens and doesn't consume any keys.
- **Home key:** a framework overlay sets `config_doubleTapOnHomeBehavior` to 1, so Android holds the
  first press for 300 ms and swallows the second. Some devices only do this while PiP is showing.
- **Guide key:** a second overlay points `KEYCODE_GUIDE` in `global_keys.xml` at this app, so the key
  is consumed before apps see it. An overlay replaces the whole table, so `customize.sh` installs
  it on `wayne` only.
- **Permissions:** the overlay also sets `config_recentsComponentName`, which grants this app the
  system's `recents` role. The app runs as a privileged system app, added systemlessly by Magisk.
- **Thumbnails:** Android disables its snapshot cache on TV devices. `takeTaskSnapshot(id, false)`
  skips that check for a visible task, so the watcher triggers a capture on the first Home press.

## Build

You need JDK 17, `curl`, `zip` and `unzip`. Builds run on macOS and Linux, without the Android SDK.

```sh
./build.sh      # writes out/tvrecents-<version>.zip
./install.sh    # installs it on the connected device and reboots
./uninstall.sh  # removes it and reboots
```

`tools/fetch-deps.sh` downloads the build tools to `.tools/` and verifies their checksums. The build
uses `dx` rather than `d8`, so don't use Java lambdas: they crash at runtime.
